title: Microsoft Purview: apply a retention policy to Microsoft Planner content
summary: Hold: the sources do not establish that existing plans remain unaffected until an administrator creates a policy. The roadmap gives group-associated plans as an example, not an exclusive scope restriction. The general retention controls and licensing are documented, and the briefing correctly reports Learn's disagreement with the roadmap.

claims.claim: The roadmap introduces Purview Data Lifecycle Management retention policies for Planner content, such as tasks in group-associated plans.
claims.quote: Compliance admins can now create a retention policy to manage content located in Microsoft Planner such as tasks for plans associated with an Microsoft 365 Group.

claims.claim: Each Planner plan lives in a container.

claims.claim: General retention settings support retain-only.
claims.quote: Retain-only: Retain content forever or for a specified period of time.

claims.claim: General delete-only retention permanently deletes content after a specified period.
claims.quote: Delete-only: Permanently delete content after a specified period of time.

claims.claim: General retention settings support retain-then-delete.
claims.quote: Retain and then delete: Retain content for a specified period of time and then permanently delete it.

claims.claim: Setting up a retention policy does not widen who can read plan content.
claims.quote: Searched: retention policies do not change permissions access content Planner. Read get-started-with-data-lifecycle-management, Planner compliance and planner-in-purview. Not requiring content access to configure a policy does not establish its effect on readership.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with "Learn says the person configuring retention policies doesn't require access to the content." Remove the inference about whether configuring a Planner policy changes who can read the content.
